segments.text: Now that we cover why safety matters, let's dive into the hazards you might face in a
lab.
Some are easy to spot, others not so much, but both can mess up your day if you're not
alert.
Labs are full of chemicals, some toxic, some flammable, and others just unpredictable.
Spills, leaks, or fires can happen in an instant if you're not paying attention.
Imagine you spill acetone, a highly flammable solvent.
Your first move?
Turn off or remove any source of ignition, ventilate, contain the spill, and keep anything
flammable away.
Quick thinking can save a whole lot of trouble.
Biological risks like pathogens and allergens are the ones you don't always see coming.
Contamination can hit fast if you're not careful.
You could be drawing blood and the needle slips.
Suddenly, you're exposed to a blood-borne pathogen, there's no time to hesitate.
Stop, contain, disinfect, and follow protocol to keep yourself and everyone safe.
Everyday risks like fires, electrical issues, or slipping on a wet floor are always lurking
in the background.
It's easy to ignore them until something happens.
You're working with a Bunsen burner and the flame gets too close to some of the chemicals.
Now your workstation's on fire.
Don't panic.
Evacuate, grab the extinguisher, and put it out before it spreads.
Fast action is key.
Radioactive materials come with serious risks.
Contamination and radiation exposure are no joke.
Handle them with extra care.
If something goes wrong with radioactive isotopes, isolate the area immediately, contain the
issue, and start decontamination to limit exposure and keep everyone safe.
Repetitive strain injuries are more common than you think.
Repeating the same motions for hours adds up, stressing your body.
If you're pipetting for hours and your setup isn't ergonomic, you'll feel it
later in your back or wrists.
Adjusting your station now can save you from serious discomfort down the road.
